sections.html:
Lake Oswego lies about 7 miles south of Portland, mostly in Clackamas County with small parts in Multnomah and Washington counties. Its center is Oswego Lake, a private lake of roughly 400 acres that the Clackamas people called Waluga, meaning wild swan.

The 2020 census counted 40,731 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,722. There were 17,134 households, 69.0 percent of homes were owner-occupied, and the median age was 47.3, so sellers often ask about estate steps and downsizing.

The city has 25 formally recognized neighborhood associations, among them Birdshill, Forest Hills, Lake Grove, Lakewood, Old Town, Palisades, Waluga, Westlake and Westridge. Use the right name when you describe the house.

The Lake Oswego Corporation owns the lake bed, which it received in 1942 from the Oregon Iron and Steel Company. Lake access comes with a membership attached to the deed, and more than 4,000 local households are shareholders or easement members.

Residents with deeded access pay annual assessments and license fees that fund safety patrols, water quality work, dredging, dam maintenance, and a boat ramp and marina. Dollar amounts are not posted publicly, so ask the corporation for current figures in writing before you list.

Public access has been argued in court. On August 1, 2019, the Oregon Supreme Court recognized a public right to enter the lake from public land, and in April 2024 a Clackamas County judge found the city had overstepped by blocking access from Millennium Plaza Park. Buyers hear about these rulings, so a lakefront seller should read the latest news before describing exclusivity in any listing.

Lake Oswego requires a permit to remove a tree with a trunk of 6 inches or more in diameter, and replacement trees are required in most cases. Under city code section 55.02, a significant tree is a healthy, non-invasive tree over 15 inches, or the only tree left on a lot.

PermitWhat it coversProcess
Type IUp to two trees of 15 inches or less per year on a residential lot with a single-family house. Does not apply within the 25-foot Oswego Lake setback.Simple permit
Type IIMost other removalsPosted sign, 14-day comment period and a tentative decision

Replacement usually means one 1.5-inch deciduous tree or one 6-foot evergreen for each tree removed, and two for a significant tree. Each unlawful removal is a separate civil violation, and a stump of eight caliper inches or more counts as prima facie evidence. Lakefront owners also answer to the Lake Oswego Corporation, whose tree policy requires a city permit and the corporation's signature for a removal of 6 inches or more from corporation land. A removal done solely for a view does not qualify under the Type II criteria. If you cleared trees recently, keep the paperwork, because a buyer's attorney may ask.

Lake Oswego owners pay Clackamas County property tax, levied by 130 taxing districts across 357 tax code areas. That patchwork is why two houses of similar value can get different bills.

The county reported that about 6.0 percent of properties paid tax on real market value, because Measure 50 limits growth of assessed value for the rest. Statewide, assessed value can rise 3 percent a year at most. Check your own account on the county site for your parcel's numbers.

Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. When the first date falls on a weekend it moves to the next business day, as it did in 2025, when it shifted to November 17. Appeals are accepted through December 31. The county's lobby is in Oregon City at 150 Beavercreek Road, Suite 135. Tell your title company which bill is current so the proration at closing is correct.

The Lake Oswego School District serves about 7,000 students through two high schools, Lake Oswego and Lakeridge, two junior highs and six elementary schools. A portion of the city lies in Portland Public Schools, and TriMet has run local bus service since 1970.

The city maintains about 600 acres of parks and open space, including George Rogers Park, Millennium Plaza Park and the Lake Oswego Golf Course. The Lake Oswego Recreation and Aquatics Center opened in 2025, and the Willamette Shore Trolley runs tourist rides on the old rail line. A short list of nearby parks and trails helps when you talk price with a buyer.

With a median age of 47.3, many Lake Oswego sellers are long-time owners selling an inherited home or moving to something smaller. Estate sales need paperwork showing who may sign, and a trust or probate step can come first. Tell the title company at the start, because it decides the order of documents.

Heirs who live elsewhere often want a single closing date they can plan around. Settle who is handling utilities, yard care and the lake fees until the deed transfers, since those bills keep arriving.

sections.h2: What Lake Oswego sellers usually deal with
sections.html:
• Lake rights: confirming that shareholder or easement status transfers, and what the annual fees are.
  • Trees: permits and replacement rules can slow a pre-sale cleanup.
  • Estates and downsizing: an older resident base brings these sales up often.
  • Tax proration: the closing statement splits the current tax year, so know which installments you have paid.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in Lake Oswego
sections.html:
A cash sale does not remove any of these items, but it lets you pick a closing date and avoid repairs, staging and showings. Title will still check lake rights and record the deed, and you should still read every number on the closing statement before you sign.

We buy houses in Lake Oswego as they are. Request an offer online or by phone, and gather your tax statement, mortgage payoff figure and lake membership papers to move things along.

faqs.q: What county is Lake Oswego in?
faqs.a: Lake Oswego is mostly in Clackamas County, with small parts in Multnomah and Washington counties. It lies about 7 miles south of Portland.

The Lake Oswego Corporation owns the lake bed, which it received in 1942. More than 4,000 households are shareholders or easement members, and those with deeded access pay annual assessments and license fees.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Lake Oswego?
faqs.a: Yes, for a tree of 6 inches in diameter or more. A Type I permit can cover up to two trees of 15 inches or less per year on a single-family residential lot, and most other removals need a Type II permit.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lake Oswego?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,722 residents. The 2020 census counted 40,731.

faqs.q: When are Clackamas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. The first date moves to the next business day when it falls on a weekend, as it did in 2025.
